READABILITY.evidence: Names say what they do (buildWindowClause, assertWindowName, WindowSpec, WindowFrameBoundary). Each dialect's .window() has a JSDoc with an example in the style of existing methods, and dprint was run. Single-letter names (q, m, s) appear only in tests.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: All spec, validation and clause logic lives in sql/functions/window.ts (~400 lines). Each dialect only adds an optional windows field, a 3-line .window() and a one-line `buildWindowClause(windows)`. It uses the sql tag, sql.join and bindIfParam, matching the project conventions.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every listed constraint is enforced with the required wording: ntile/nthValue name and value, preceding/following name, from-after-to check, non-empty and whitespace window names. Numeric args go into the SQL text, not params, and that includes 0. Nothing is caught or swallowed, and the hidden tests pass 130/130.

C6-02-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive: `windows?: { name: string; spec: WindowSpec }[]` is optional on all five *SelectConfig types, and the same `window(name, spec = {}): this` exists on the pg, mysql, sqlite, gel and singlestore builders. windowSql is undefined when no windows are set, and the 566 existing (P2P) tests pass.
